searchText: I doubt it was ever really implemented anywhere since it was wip, and it's being deprecated for the next version https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/pull/227/ hmm so no built in security anymore? how does ethereum protect the discovery layer then? I thought we had at least this there are several security measures in place, so it depends on the security concerns you have for example the ticketing system made a bit hard to overflow a certain topic with sybils due to waiting times now what is the sybil protection for topics? btw why is it deprecated? I understand that it was far from perfect but it was still something topics were part of the whole idea, they were not implemented and are not currently in use as far as I know subnet peer discovery is done via random walk finding enrs that advertise subnets, not via topics advertise in their enr fields* thanks so let's take sybils in general what is the current protection? just the number of different IPs the attacker must hold? it doesn't seem to be part of the spec but not just different ips but ips across /24 subnets the best person for your questions is probably <@194432762315407360> We have some mechanisms in place, but it is mostly implementation details. There are the IP limits and some specific validation rules that should be in all implementations. There is no general solution to the sybil problem The way I see it, we can only attempt to ensure nodes in discovery are reachable and behave according to protocol The discovery protocol is a public database of all existing nodes It should be reasonably hard to enlist totally fake information In order to be shared by other nodes, a node must be reachable on the signed endpoint they are advertising. Our validation rules should guarantee that. If you put in the effort to add sybils into the network, the question would be what you'd even get for that you can rent lots of cheap vps each for a few dollars apiece and perform some eclipses on the dht I guess but what would that give you then? the way we have the dht set up, it's a source of connectivity but not the only source so yeah, you can cause some trouble, but ultimately your fake nodes will need to serve verifiable chain information there are other sources? manual peering? if you want to grief a specific validator, you'd need to know their node ID and also perform an attack tailored to the implementation which is used that's on the pubsub layer, no? or you connect the 2? what I'm trying to say is, attacking the discovery for the purpose of attacking discovery is pointless the discovery protocol is a means to find other nodes to talk to about blockchain information I mean the network would continue to function, no doubt it will just cause troubles like you said... newcomers will have issues regarding the discovery options, I am very confident that larger validator deployments use manual peering for safety reasons they'd always do that there is also the option of using EIP-1459 DNS node lists, which can be set up in a web-of-trust like way anyway, the basic point you made is correct. there is no special mechanism to guard against sybil attacks. if you have good ideas for adding security to the network, please do share them the ticket stuff is a great idea, and we are still pursuing it for the topic index, but it's not active right now not really there is the [proof of validator](https://ethresear.ch/t/proof-of-validator-a-simple-anonymous-credential-scheme-for-ethereums-dht/16454) idea that sounds nice I liked the ticketing idea... sure it wasn't perfect but it was something glad to see you are still pursuing it yeah I checked the proof of validator it's a cool idea but I think not generally applicable for all nodes another option would be putting a node list on the blockchain, allowing anyone to list their node for a fee this could operate alongside the existing mechanisms this may open up attack vector if many honest operators would just cheap out on paying the fee and attackers will agree to pay? wasn't really meant to be a fully thought out proposal, but yeah, there are some issues with it a general issue is that nodes usually do not have a lof of intrinsic interest to be discovered so why would they pay for it > There is no general solution to the sybil problem It is getting late for me in my TZ and I don't think I will come up now with a good solution but if I will have some interesting ideas I will come back here and tag you 🙂 actually kicking out nodes with bad pubsub scores from the dht is not bad I think maybe? yeah this is getting into the implementation details you're doing this? so it's feasible for an implementation to do this in go-ethereum, which I work on, we don't aite I am not even totally sure it is a good idea sounds good at least I guess I personally think it's pointless because the attacker has infinite attempts the value of a specific node ID is very low yeah having scores in the system changes this a bit, because the node may have to behave good for a while in order to get a good score but then again it's not hard to game and scoring has other problems as well, which is why we don't really do it in EL networking but I know some of the CLs have it aite goodnight for real now 🙂

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: We have some mechanisms in place, but it is mostly implementation details. There are the IP limits and some specific validation rules that should be in all implementations.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: There is no general solution to the sybil problem

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The way I see it, we can only attempt to ensure nodes in discovery are reachable and behave according to protocol

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The discovery protocol is a public database of all existing nodes

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: It should be reasonably hard to enlist totally fake information

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: In order to be shared by other nodes, a node must be reachable on the signed endpoint they are advertising. Our validation rules should guarantee that.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: If you put in the effort to add sybils into the network, the question would be what you'd even get for that
